subject: E-Commerce
title: The Survivors
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Survivors usable.

hook.text: Amazon nearly died in 2001. Its stock fell 94% and analysts said it would run out of cash by Christmas.

buildup.text: After the crash, only companies with real revenue survived. Amazon, eBay, and Priceline made the cut.

discovery.text: Amazon survived by raising $672 million in convertible bonds just before the crash. Timing saved it.

twist.text: The crash created a talent surplus. Suddenly top engineers were cheap. Survivors hired aggressively.

climax.text: By 2003, e-commerce was growing again—but only for disciplined companies with real unit economics.

punchline.text: Stock down 94%, nearly dead. Amazon survived and conquered everything.

quiz.question: How did Amazon survive the dot-com crash?
options: Raised $672M in bonds just before the crash
